column3: The Hebrew links the guardians directly with Ahab without separately repeating his sons.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “with you” for the equipment.
The Hebrew uses good and upright; BSB has the best and most worthy.
The Hebrew repeats “very” and uses an ordinary saying verb without a conditional if; BSB has being terrified and reasoning conditionally.
The Hebrew explicitly says whatever you say “to us.”
The Hebrew leaves Jehu unnamed and names taking the heads and coming as separate commands. His voice is explicit; BSB condenses these as bringing the heads and obeying him.
The Hebrew leaves the recipient unnamed; BSB supplies Jehu.
The Hebrew leaves both recipient and speaker unnamed; BSB names Jehu twice.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and uses striking for the final deaths; BSB names Jehu and uses killing.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD three times and retains falling to earth and the servant’s hand; BSB uses failing and through.
The Hebrew uses a striking verb; BSB renders it killed.
The Hebrew has three separate movement verbs and leaves the traveler unnamed; BSB supplies Jehu and condenses setting out.
The Hebrew calls them brothers, without a separate “some”; BSB calls them some relatives.
The Hebrew leaves speaker and captors unnamed; BSB supplies Jehu and his men.
The Hebrew uses a blessing verb and repeatedly leaves Jehu unnamed; BSB has greeting and explicitly names Jehu.
The Hebrew has plural agents making him ride; BSB uses singular he.
The Hebrew repeats Samaria and has singular him as the object of destruction; BSB uses there and them.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says to consecrate an assembly; BSB has proclaiming it.
The Hebrew repeats Baal’s house and retains mouth to mouth as its fullness image; BSB uses a pronoun and end to end.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed; BSB supplies Jehu.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed after naming the arrivals; BSB explicitly repeats Jehu.
The Hebrew has singular soul for soul; BSB renders this as forfeiting his life for theirs.
The Hebrew names the mouth of the sword and the city of Baal’s house; BSB uses putting to the sword and an inner room.
The Hebrew names pillars in the plural, then uses a singular object pronoun for burning; BSB has one pillar.
The Hebrew repeats demolishing and uses plural privies; BSB varies tore down and latrine.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Jehu; BSB uses he and supplies worship.
The Hebrew begins with and, without explicit Nevertheless.
